text: The doctor did a great job, the clinic was clean, and the service was good. However, the assistant was clumsy and made mistakes while suctioning, releasing fluid incorrectly and frantically. I felt sorry for both the doctor and myself, as it made the doctor's job difficult. I experienced pain from multiple suction attempts on my lips, and fluid was even spilled on my head and nose. But thankfully, I survived. Keep up the good work, assistant!

restaurant_name: Dent Indeed Dental clinic คลินิกทันตกรรมเดนท์ อินดี๊ด
text: My mother told me that during her dental visit, the assistant was suctioning saliva and blood from her mouth, but didn't suction everything out, causing the procedure to stop midway because my mother was choking repeatedly. After a while, the assistant said to my mother, "Is your nose blocked? Can't you breathe through your nose? Bear with it. If you keep stopping like this, it'll never be finished." How can someone speak to a customer like that? If they don't have a service-oriented mindset, they shouldn't be working in customer service. If I come back next time, I'll say this: I want to meet them again. They should have suctioned all the saliva to prevent the customer from choking and avoid frequent stops. To say something like that... what does that even mean?
